_README: Verdicts for every runtime GC-pointer holder that scripts/gc_runtime_root_holders.py
enumerates and finds NOT reached by a registered root scanner in its own file (#7231).
An entry that matches no such holder FAILS the gate. That is deliberate: it is what
makes a fix delete its own entry, and it is why 'covered_elsewhere' is a verdict rather
than a suppression — if the scanner that covers it is ever deleted, the holder stays
uncovered, the entry stays matched, and nothing tells you. Read the named scanner if you
covered_elsewhere  - a REGISTERED scanner visits it, but from a different file, so the
same-file rule cannot see it. `scanner` names it. These are the
gate's known false positives, recorded rather than silenced.
not_a_gc_pointer   - the stored value is an id, a counter, an epoch, a code address, a
.rodata object, or Rust-owned state. Nothing for the collector.
test_only          - #[cfg(test)] storage; never live in a shipped binary.
open_gap           - a real unrooted GC pointer. `issue` says where it is tracked; this
verdict FAILS while old-page relocation ships enabled.
unverified         - enumerated, verdict NOT established. This also FAILS: an unknown
movable-address contract cannot be a production exemption.

holders.name: NEXT_ID
holders.why: Monotonic backoff-state id counter (lib.rs:378). The closures live in STATES (BackoffState.task/outer/retry_cb), which scan_backoff_roots visits.

holders.name: REQUEST_HANDLES
holders.scanner: gc::scan_fetch_roots (crates/perry-ext-fetch/src/gc.rs), registered via perry_ffi::gc_register_mutable_root_scanner_named from gc::ensure_gc_scanner_registered, armed at store_request before the first insert
holders.why: Declared in lib.rs, scanned from the gc.rs submodule (split out for the 2,000-line gate): every RequestRecord.signal slot is visited and rewritten.

holders.name: HTTP_PENDING_EVENTS
holders.why: Client-side pending-event queue. Every variant carries a perry-ffi registry Handle, strings, Bytes, or an errno i64 (rule S fired on TransportError.errno) — no NaN-boxed value. The closures the drain fires live in ClientRequestHandle (response_callback/end_callback/pending_write_callbacks/listeners), which scan_http_roots visits.

holders.name: PENDING_TLS_CLIENT_ERRORS
holders.why: Vec<PendingTlsClientError>: an i64 server HANDLE (an index into the handle side table, stable across collection -- not a heap address) plus an owned Rust String. Neither field can hold a pointer into the GC heap, so there is nothing for a scanner to visit.

holders.name: PENDING_TLS_KEYLOGS
holders.why: Vec<PendingTlsKeylog>: an i64 server HANDLE plus Vec<Vec<u8>> of owned keylog bytes. Both are Rust-allocated; no JS heap pointer is stored, so no root scanner is required.

holders.name: CONNECTIONS
holders.why: TrackedConnection = {server_handle: ffi registry id, close: Notify, busy/read_active: atomics}. No JS values; server closures live in the HttpServer handle, scanned by scan_http_server_roots.

holders.name: PENDING_CONNECTION_EVENTS
holders.why: Vec of server-handle registry ids drained by js_node_http_server_process_pending to fire 'connection' listeners; the listeners themselves are in HttpServer.listeners, scanned by scan_http_server_roots.

holders.name: IN_FLIGHT
holders.why: InFlightRequest = three perry-ffi registry handle ids + a deadline Instant. The JS-value-bearing objects behind the ids (IncomingMessage/ServerResponse) are registered handles scanned by scan_http_server_roots via iter_handles_of_mut.

holders.name: P
holders.why: pending_events(): Vec<PendingNetEvent>; every variant carries socket/server ids, Bytes, String, bool, or DropInfo (SocketAddrs) — no closures or NaN-boxed values. Listener closures live in listeners(), visited by scan_net_roots.

holders.name: SCRATCH
holders.why: Drain-side reusable Vec<PendingNetEvent> inside js_ext_net_drain_pending; same payload as P (ids/Bytes/strings), emptied within the drain call. No JS values.

holders.name: STATE
holders.why: ConnectionOrderState = socket-id VecDeques, per-server usize credits, and buffered Bytes chunks keyed by socket id. Pure ids and bytes; no NaN-boxed values.

holders.name: ABORTS
holders.why: HashSet<i64> of pending TLS abort handles. Each i64 is a socket HANDLE -- the key used to look the socket up in crate::statics::sockets() and the payload of PendingNetEvent::AbortError/Close -- i.e. an index into the handle side table, stable across collection, not a heap address. The set holds no other field, so there is nothing for a scanner to visit.

holders.name: PENDING
holders.why: Pending watcher events carry only a subscription u64 id plus Rust-owned PathBuf/String payloads and enum tags. Callback closures live in perry-ffi CallbackRoot handles, which scan_subscription_roots visits and rewrites.

holders.name: WARNED
holders.why: HashSet of perry-ffi registry handle ids already found stale, kept only to log each once. Registry ids are indices into the ffi DashMap, not heap addresses.

holders.name: ASYNC_HOOK_HANDLES
holders.why: HashSet of Box::into_raw AsyncHookHandle pointers allocated by Rust's global allocator, outside Perry's GC heap. The boxes are never freed or moved; membership is used only to recognize dynamic AsyncHook receivers.

holders.name: ASYNC_HOOK_HANDLE_COUNT
holders.why: Monotonic count of AsyncHookHandle boxes registered in ASYNC_HOOK_HANDLES. It holds no address and is used only as a fast-path emptiness check.

holders.name: ASYNC_RESOURCE_HANDLES
holders.why: HashSet of async resource IDs (async_hooks' asyncId space), not heap addresses. The resource OBJECTS live in RESOURCES, which scan_async_hooks_roots_mut visits.

holders.name: ASYNC_RESOURCE_HANDLE_COUNT
holders.why: Monotonic counter of live async-resource handles. Holds no address at all; the resource objects live in RESOURCES, which scan_async_hooks_roots_mut visits.

holders.name: TEST_FORCE_RESOLVE_GC
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] AtomicUsize one-shot flag that asks resolve_async_resource_handle to force a collection; stores only 0 or 1 and is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: BUFFER_ADDR_RANGE
holders.why: Records only the smallest and largest address ever inserted into the sibling thread-local buffer registry, as a conservative min/max filter in front of that registry's hash lookup (#9176). The two usizes are compared (`addr >= lo && addr <= hi`) and never dereferenced, never handed out, and never used to reach an object; a value outside the range is rejected, a value inside falls through to the lookup that was already there. The range only ever widens, so it cannot go stale in the unsafe direction: a bound that no longer matches reality can only admit more addresses to the real lookup, never deny a registered one.

holders.name: CP_NEXT_LIVE_ID
holders.why: Monotonic id counter for CP_LIVE keys. CP_LIVE itself is covered by cp_reactor_scan_roots_mut.

holders.name: CAPTURED_MISS_STREAK
holders.why: Keyed by the closure's func_ptr — a CODE address, which the collector neither moves nor traces; the value is a miss-streak count.

holders.name: CLOSURE_CAP_SINGLETON_HIT
holders.why: Cache hit counter (telemetry). Holds no address.

holders.name: CLOSURE_CAP_SINGLETON_MISS
holders.why: Cache miss counter (telemetry). Holds no address.

holders.name: CLOSURE_VERSIONED_LOOP_REGISTRY
holders.why: Maps a closure body `func_ptr` (a code pointer, never moved) to TrustedDirectTarget{func_ptr:*const u8, capture_count:u32, boxed_capture_mask:u64}. Both key and value are code pointers and plain integers; no field can hold a heap pointer, so the table cannot hold a GC root. Same shape as its sibling CLOSURE_ARROW_FUNCTION_REGISTRY in the same thread_local block.

holders.name: NEXT_READ_LINES_ID
holders.why: Monotonic id counter for READ_LINES_REGISTRY keys. The registry's own heap values are visited by scan_filehandle_roots_mut (fs/filehandle.rs:65), reached from scan_fs_handle_roots_mut.

holders.name: MAP_FOREACH_STACK
holders.why: Holds Set/Map header ADDRESSES as identity keys for in-flight forEach walks (#9082); the values are only ever compared (`contains`, `pop` equality) and truncated, never dereferenced, so no collector edge originates here. Correctness across evacuation is maintained by set_header_moved_for_gc / map_header_moved_for_gc, which rewrite every matching entry when a header moves — see the SET_FOREACH_STACK/MAP_FOREACH_STACK rewrite loops there.

holders.name: TCP_SERVERS
holders.why: Keyed by handle id; TcpListenerWrapper is Rust-owned (tokio listener + SocketAddr), no JS values.

holders.name: TCP_SOCKETS
holders.why: Keyed by handle id; TcpStreamWrapper is Rust-owned (tokio stream + SocketAddr), no JS values.

holders.name: LEGACY_CAPTURE
holders.why: Temporary legacy-addon registration state: a canonical Rust PathBuf, a pointer to the addon's static napi_module descriptor in the loaded native library, and counters/flags. It never stores a Perry GC-heap address.

holders.name: PENDING_FINALIZERS
holders.why: Queue entries contain a native addon function pointer plus the addon's opaque data and hint pointers. Node-API defines those as embedder-owned native pointers; no field is a Perry GC-heap address.

holders.name: FILE_BLOB_STREAMS
holders.why: Keyed by stream id; FileBlobStreamState is Rust-owned (byte buffers + offsets), no JS values.

holders.name: NEXT_FILE_BLOB_STREAM_ID
holders.why: Monotonic id counter.

holders.name: DIAG_CHANNELS
holders.why: Visited from the sibling module, so the same-file rule misses it.

holders.name: DIAG_NOOP_CLOSURE
holders.why: Visited from the sibling module.

holders.name: DIAG_TRACES
holders.why: Visited from the sibling module, so the same-file rule misses it. The `events: [i64; 5]` are DIAG_CHANNELS ids, not addresses.

holders.name: DIAG_STORE_SCOPES
holders.why: DiagStoreScopeState.handles are store KEYS produced by store_handle() (diagnostics_tail.rs:72), which admits only an INT32-tagged value, a POINTER_TAG value inside the handle band (raw < 0x10000), or a finite float — a real heap pointer returns None, so one cannot be stored here by construction. The store CONTEXT objects live in DIAG_CHANNELS[*].stores, which scan_node_submodule_singleton_roots_mut visits.

holders.name: VM_INTRINSIC_GLOBAL
holders.scanner: gc::roots::visit_global_root_slots, reached by js_gc_register_global_root (gc/roots.rs:325 pushes the slot into GLOBAL_ROOTS; gc/roots.rs:1433 hands it to the mutable-root walk)
holders.why: Caches the shared VM intrinsic realm's globalThis as NaN-boxed bits. The single site that writes the cell — fresh_intrinsic_global, node_vm.rs:1080 — calls js_gc_register_global_root(slot.as_ptr()) in the same `with` closure, immediately after the store and with no allocation in between; the early return on a non-zero cell means that store happens at most once per thread, so there is no path that populates the cell without registering it. GLOBAL_ROOTS is thread_local, exactly like the cell, and visit_mutable_root_slots feeds it to BOTH the marker and the post-evacuation rewrite (gc/tests/copying.rs:1272, test_copying_minor_rewrites_shadow_and_global_roots), so the cached pointer is marked and forwarded rather than left stale.

holders.name: CLASS_OBJECT_VALUES
holders.scanner: object::scan_class_side_table_roots_mut and its budgeted step twin (class_registry/gc_roots.rs:138 and :256)
holders.why: The class side tables are declared in state.rs and scanned from gc_roots.rs. Both twins visit it — #7239 diffed all eight budgeted (FULL, STEP) pairs and found no drift.

holders.name: CLASS_STATIC_PROTOTYPES
holders.scanner: object::class_registry::gc_roots::scan_class_side_table_roots_mut and its budgeted step twin (class_side_table_root_snapshot enumerates ClassSideTableRootSlot::StaticPrototype; scan_class_side_table_root_slot visits that slot)
holders.why: Constructor-side [[Prototype]] recorded by Object.setPrototypeOf(Ctor, obj) on a declared class. Holds a real heap ObjectHeader address as usize, so it is visited with visit_usize_slot in BOTH the full and budgeted class-side-table walks, exactly like the CLASS_DECL_PROTOTYPE_OBJECTS entries beside it, and class_static_prototype_root_store fires runtime_write_barrier_root_raw_ptr on the stored pointer.

holders.name: CLASS_STATIC_PROTOTYPE_NULLED
holders.why: Set of class ids whose constructor [[Prototype]] was explicitly set to null, so Object.getPrototypeOf answers null rather than the default Function.prototype. Stores u32 class ids only — no heap address, nothing to trace or forward.

holders.name: CLASS_SYMBOL_MEMBER_ORDERS
holders.why: Source order for Symbol-keyed class members: HashMap<(class_id, SymbolHeader::id, is_static), u32>. The u64 is the symbol's stable id (read once at registration in record_class_symbol_member_order), NOT its address, so the table needs no re-key when a Symbol is evacuated; the value is an order index. The member values themselves live in CLASS_SYMBOL_METHODS/CLASS_SYMBOL_ACCESSORS, which scan_class_symbol_member_keys_mut visits and rewrite_class_symbol_method_key_if_forwarded re-keys.

holders.name: TEST_TRANSITION_FAST_HITS
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] hit counter for the learned shape-transition fast path: a thread_local Cell<u64> incremented on each hit and reset by test_reset_transition_fast_hits. Holds a count, never a JSValue or heap pointer, and does not exist in a release build.

holders.name: TEST_COLLECT_BEFORE_GLOBAL_THIS_ALLOC
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] Cell<bool> one-shot flag that asks js_get_global_this to collect once before it allocates the realm, so the unresolved-global rooting regression can observe the relocation; stores only true/false and is absent from shipped binaries.

holders.name: THREAD_GLOBAL_THIS
holders.scanner: gc::roots GLOBAL_ROOTS — the cell's address is registered with js_gc_register_global_root (fetch_globals.rs, js_get_global_this) and marked+rewritten as a mutable global root
holders.why: A raw-pointer cache slot registered as a global root at first population; the registration is a call, not a scanner body, so the walk cannot see it.

holders.name: THREAD_MODULE_TOP_THIS
holders.scanner: gc::roots GLOBAL_ROOTS — the cell's address is registered with js_gc_register_global_root (fetch_globals.rs, js_module_top_this)
holders.why: Same shape as THREAD_GLOBAL_THIS: a NaN-boxed cache slot registered as a mutable global root at first population.

holders.name: CLASS_DYNAMIC_PROP_ORDER
holders.why: First-insertion order for CLASS_DYNAMIC_PROPS: HashMap<class_id, Vec<String>> of owned Rust strings, needed because the value table is a HashMap while [[OwnPropertyKeys]] needs order. Holds no JSValues; the f64 values live in CLASS_DYNAMIC_PROPS, which is already a scanned root.

holders.name: TEST_BOUND_METHOD_MOVE
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] diagnostic trace for the bound-method moving-GC regression: records the (before, after) addresses a test-forced minor produced so the test can assert the relocation happened. The addresses are compared as integers, never dereferenced, and the cell is dead in a shipped binary.

holders.name: READ_STUB
holders.why: Megamorphic property-read stub cache, the read twin of WRITE_STUB: 2-way ways of (shape_token, key_bits, slot) plain u64s. The token is a shape id and the slot an index; key_bits are content-derived by construction, because read_stub_key_bits returns short_ascii_sso_bits(key) — the key's characters packed inline — and yields None for any key that would otherwise be stored under a pointer. No way holds a heap address, so nothing here keeps an object alive, and a stale entry cannot hit: receiver_shape_token returns None for a receiver with no live shape, and the token identifies the exact key set and order, so a shape change yields a different token.

holders.name: SIGNAL_ASYNC_IDS
holders.why: Maps owned Rust signal-name strings to async_hooks async IDs. Async IDs are scalar u64 identifiers, not JS heap addresses; the AsyncResource objects themselves live in async_hooks RESOURCES, whose registered scanner visits them.

holders.name: LOOP_START_MS
holders.why: A timeOrigin-relative millisecond timestamp (or the -1 'loop has not started' sentinel) reported as nodeTiming.loopStart, and the gate eventLoopUtilization() reads before reporting anything but zeros. An f64 time value, never an address.

holders.name: MODULE_LOADER_NEXT_LOAD
holders.why: Same scanner, same file split.

holders.name: MODULE_LOADER_NEXT_RESOLVE
holders.why: Declared in process.rs, scanned from the process/node_module.rs submodule.

holders.name: PROCESS_FINALIZATION_BEFORE_EXIT_LISTENER
holders.scanner: process::scan_process_finalization_roots_mut (process/finalization.rs:171; visits the cell at :184-189 via visit_raw_const_ptr_slot; reg_scanner! at gc/mod.rs:1008)
holders.why: Declared in process.rs, scanned from the process/finalization.rs submodule — same file split as the MODULE_LOADER_* siblings.

holders.name: ASYNC_BOX_EXECUTION_REF_BASES
holders.why: Vec<u32> of checked length snapshots from ASYNC_BOX_EXECUTION_REFS. Every entry comes only from Vec::len() and is used only as a later Vec drain boundary; no address or JS value can enter this vector, and entries are never dereferenced or decoded.

holders.name: CURRENT_MICROTASK_VALUE
holders.scanner: promise::scan_promise_roots_mut (promise/scanners.rs:66, visit_cell_f64_slot) plus its budgeted step twin scan_current_microtask_value_step (scanners.rs:420); registered via reg_budgeted_scanner! at gc/mod.rs:833-838
holders.why: Declared in promise/microtasks.rs, scanned from promise/scanners.rs. The scanners.rs:786/913 sites are the mutator-side save/clear the scanner exists to protect, not the coverage mechanism.

holders.name: WRITE_STUB
holders.why: Megamorphic dynamic-write stub cache: 4096 ways of (shape_token, key_bits, slot) plain u64s. The token is a shape id and the slot an index; key_bits are content-derived by construction, because stub_key_bits admits only SSO immediates (and short ASCII heap strings folded to the SSO bits of their content) and rejects every key that would otherwise be stored under a pointer. No way holds a heap address, so nothing here keeps an object alive, and a stale entry is rejected by dyn_ic_try_store's per-hit shape-token/flags/slot-bound revalidation.

holders.name: EXIT_SINK
holders.why: #[cfg(test)] sink for the pty exit callback's two JSValues. Never compiled into a shipped binary.

holders.name: REGEX_POINTERS
holders.scanner: regex::regex_header_moved_for_gc / regex_header_clear_dead_for_gc (regex.rs), the RegExp move/death hooks the copying minor and sweep invoke
holders.why: Address-KEYED owner set, not a root: the key is rekeyed when the RegExpHeader moves and removed when it dies; it never keeps the header alive. Reached from GC hooks, not from a registered scanner, so the walk misses it.

holders.name: REGEX_SOURCE_TABLE
holders.why: Address-KEYED owner table (owned String copies of pattern/flags); rekeyed on move, cleared on death, same hooks as REGEX_POINTERS.

holders.name: VALIDATED_PATTERNS
holders.why: Memoises which (pattern, flags) pairs have already passed the eager syntax check, so a repeated literal validates once (#9178). Keys are owned Rust `String`s copied out of the JS strings, and the value is `()` — nothing in the map is or points to a JS heap object, so there is no slot for the collector to mark or rewrite. The JS string a pattern came from is rooted by its own RegExp header, independently of this table.

holders.name: SET_FOREACH_STACK
holders.why: Holds Set/Map header ADDRESSES as identity keys for in-flight forEach walks (#9082); the values are only ever compared (`contains`, `pop` equality) and truncated, never dereferenced, so no collector edge originates here. Correctness across evacuation is maintained by set_header_moved_for_gc / map_header_moved_for_gc, which rewrite every matching entry when a header moves — see the SET_FOREACH_STACK/MAP_FOREACH_STACK rewrite loops there.

holders.name: SET_INDEX
holders.why: Derived cache of the Set's own elements array, which is the canonical scanned storage (GcRewriteDescriptorKind::Set element-slot walk). Not root-scanner-shaped: the outer address key is rekeyed on relocation by GcMoveHookKind::SetSideTables -> set_header_moved_for_gc (set.rs:352), the JSValueKey inner keys are rebuilt post-rewrite by GcRewriteHookKind::SetIndex -> rebuild_set_index_for_gc (set.rs:315, fired from gc/copying.rs:669/798, gc/barrier/mod.rs:195, gc/verify.rs:114), and finalize_set_side_allocation_for_gc (set.rs:374) prunes dead owners — the same three-hook design as MAP_INDEX.

holders.name: POW10
holders.why: A [u64; 7] constant table of powers of ten.

holders.name: PERRY_EMPTY_STRING
holders.why: A StringHeader living in .rodata, not in the arena. It has no GcHeader, is never allocated and never moves; the collector's heap-attribution predicates reject its address.

holders.name: CACHED
holders.why: Memoizes the sym_key of the Symbol.for('NextInternalRequestMeta') REGISTERED symbol. Registered / well-known symbols are Box::leak'd (symbol.rs's SYMBOL_REGISTRY / WELL_KNOWN_SYMBOLS), so they live outside the GC arena and their addresses are stable for the process. A FRESH Symbol() would not be — see #7246.

holders.name: DECODER_REGISTRY
holders.why: Keyed by decoder handle id; DecoderState is Rust-owned (encoding enum, label, flags), no JS values.

holders.name: ACTIVE_THREAD_JOBS
holders.why: In-flight job counter for perry/thread.

holders.name: TIMER_HANDLE_KINDS
holders.why: Maps scalar timer handle IDs to the CallbackTimerKind enum so clearTimeout/clearInterval can destroy the matching async_hooks resource. Neither the i64 keys nor the enum values contain a JS heap address.

holders.name: FORM_DATA_REGISTRY
holders.why: Keyed by fetch handle id; FormDataStore is Rust-owned (Vec<(String, String)>). The bound-method closures for FormData live in FORM_DATA_METHOD_VALUE_CACHE, which fetch::gc::scan_fetch_roots_with visits.

holders.name: BLOB_REGISTRY
holders.why: Keyed by fetch handle id; BlobData is Rust-owned (bytes, content type, file name, last-modified). No JS values.

holders.name: FETCH_RESPONSES
holders.why: Keyed by fetch handle id; FetchResponse is Rust-owned (status, HeadersStore, body bytes, cached HANDLE IDS for headers/body stream). No JS values.

holders.name: REQUEST_REGISTRY

holders.why: RequestRecord.signal is the AbortSignal object behind request.signal (#8163). Visited from the child module, so the same-file rule misses it; everything else in the record is Rust-owned.

holders.name: STREAM_HANDLES
holders.why: Keyed by stream id; StreamState is Rust-owned (status, buffered lines, error String).

holders.name: NEXT_OBJECT_URL_ID
holders.why: Monotonic id counter.

holders.name: OBJECT_URL_REGISTRY
holders.why: blob: URL string -> Blob HANDLE ID (a fetch-band small integer), not an address.

holders.name: N
holders.why: Five identically-named per-function AtomicUsize call counters inside streams.rs (one entry covers all five: this inventory keys on file+name). Telemetry, no JS values.

holders.name: READABLE_STREAMS

holders.name: TEE_PULLING

holders.name: TRANSFORM_BACKPRESSURED_JOBS

holders.name: TRANSFORM_PENDING_WRITES

holders.name: NEXT_PORT_ID

holders.name: NEXT_WORKER_ID

holders.name: NEXT_WS_ID
holders.why: Monotonic ws id counter.

holders.name: WS_CLIENT_PARENT_SERVER
holders.why: Client ws id -> parent server HANDLE id. No address.

holders.name: WS_CONNECTIONS
holders.why: Keyed by ws id; WsConnection is Rust-owned (command sender, buffered message Strings, state flags). Listener closures live in WS_CLIENT_LISTENERS, which scan_ws_roots_mut visits.

holders.name: PENDING_CONFIG
holders.why: AppConfig is pre-launch native UI configuration: Rust strings, dimensions, flags, and widget handles; it retains no JavaScript value.

holders.name: NEXT_KEY
holders.why: NEXT_KEY is a monotonic numeric id/counter used to address native or callback-registry state; it is never a NaN-boxed JavaScript value.

holders.name: DRAG_KEYS

holders.name: CONTEXT_MENUS

holders.name: MENUS

holders.name: KEYS
holders.why: Native event-routing index made only of observer/control identities, callback-registry keys, and numeric Perry widget handles; it stores no JavaScript value.

holders.name: SHEETS

holders.name: SLIDER_BINDINGS

holders.name: TEXTFIELD_BINDINGS
holders.why: TextFieldBinding stores a native text-field handle and a Rust reentrancy flag; no JavaScript value is retained.

holders.name: TEXT_BINDINGS

holders.name: WIDGETS
holders.why: Widget registry contains native HWND objects, layout/style scalars, and numeric child handles. JavaScript callbacks are kept in scanned tables.

holders.name: NAV_STACKS
holders.why: Navigation state contains Rust page titles and numeric widget handles/indices only; no JavaScript value is retained.

holders.name: COMPLETED
holders.why: HashMap<usize, RenderCompletion> of finished PDF page renders. The key is a monotonic request id from an AtomicUsize counter, not a heap address, and RenderCompletion holds only owned Rust data (the encoded PNG bytes as Vec<u8>, or an error String). No field can hold a pointer into the GC heap, so there is nothing for a scanner to visit.

holders.name: PDFS
holders.why: PDF state contains a Rust path, numeric page indices/counts, and a zoom scalar; it stores no JavaScript value.

holders.name: TOOLTIPS
holders.why: Rich-tooltip binding retains native UI objects, widget handles, and a numeric delay/token; it contains no JavaScript callback or heap value.

holders.name: SCROLL_STATES
holders.why: ScrollState contains native pixel offsets, viewport/content sizes, and an optional numeric child widget handle only.

holders.name: DECORATION_VALUES
holders.why: Text-decoration cache pairs numeric widget handles with an integer decoration enum; it contains no JavaScript value.

holders.name: HWND_TO_HANDLE
holders.why: Native event-routing index made only of observer/control identities, callback-registry keys, and numeric Perry widget handles; it stores no JavaScript value.

holders.name: TEXT_IDS
holders.why: Text registry maps Rust string ids to numeric native widget handles; it contains no JavaScript value.

holders.name: NODES
holders.why: Tree node storage contains Rust ids/labels and numeric child-node handles only; selection callbacks live in separately scanned storage.

holders.name: HWND_TO_HANDLE
holders.why: Native event-routing index made only of observer/control identities, callback-registry keys, and numeric Perry widget handles; it stores no JavaScript value.

holders.name: HWND_TO_WINDOW
holders.why: Native event-routing index made only of observer/control identities, callback-registry keys, and numeric Perry widget handles; it stores no JavaScript value.

holders.name: WINDOW_ROOTS
holders.why: Window-root registry maps numeric window handles to numeric root-widget handles; neither value is a JavaScript heap pointer.

_FRONTIER_README: Identity-pinned debt ratchet over new perry-ui* candidates and otherwise-unclassified core perry_thread_local! declarations (see the census docstring, “The identity-pinned frontier”). A new uncovered holder fails until it is scanned, receives a researched holders verdict, or is deliberately pinned as debt. Moving a researched false positive to holders graduates it from this list. A fixed or classified holder makes its old frontier pin stale, so the receipt must be deleted.

frontier.name: PRIVATE_MEMBER_ACCESS_HINTS
frontier.why: RefCell<Vec<PrivateMemberAccessHint>>; the struct is class_id: u32, name: String, kind: u32, is_static: bool, is_write: bool -- all owned Rust data. No JSValue, NaN-box word or raw heap pointer is stored.

frontier.name: PRIVATE_METHOD_OWNER_HINT
frontier.why: RefCell<Option<(u32, String)>>: a declaring class_id plus an OWNED Rust String naming the private method. Neither field is, or is derived from, a heap address, so a copying collection cannot invalidate it and there is nothing for a scanner to visit.

frontier.name: DERIVED_SUPER_BINDING_STACK
frontier.why: RefCell<Vec<usize>> of `slot as usize`, where slot is the derived constructor's own i1 ALLOCA (perry-codegen expr/this_super_call.rs::push_shared_super_called_slot). That is a NATIVE STACK address, not a heap address: native frames do not move under GC, so this is not the address-keyed side-table shape the census exists to catch. The only accesses are slot.read() / slot.write(1) on that one-byte has-super()-run flag. Lifetime is bounded by the js_derived_super_scope_push/pop pair around the constructor body plus the savepoint/restore pairs in exception.rs:224/349 and class_registry/dispatch.rs:540/550, so no entry outlives its frame.

frontier.name: REPEAT_MATCHER_CACHE
frontier.why: HashMap<(String,String), Arc<RepeatMatcherRegex>> -- owned Rust strings keying an Arc to a compiled matcher. No JS heap pointer, so nothing asks a scanner to visit it.
